text:
jane (customer): Hi team — we started getting 429s this morning during short bursts. quota UI shows we have quota left. Happens mainly on POST /v1/generate. Example: spike to ~100 rps for 20-40s, then many 429s. Any ideas?

alex: Sorry you're hitting this, jane. A couple quick Qs: are you on hosted Redwood API or a Dedicated deployment? Can you paste a minimal curl (with obfuscated keys) and one 429 response body? Also helpful: the X-Request-ID from response headers.

jane (customer): Hosted. Here's a repro curl (redacted):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model": "redwood-large-1", "input": "summarize: ...", "max_tokens": 256}'
```

And the error body we got repeatedly: 

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "message": "Rate limit exceeded for requests per second",
    "retry_after_seconds": 2
  }
}
```

Response headers included `x-redwood-request-id: rwd_abc123` and `x-rate-limit-remaining: 12` at first, then 0 when it flipped.

alex: Thanks. Two likely causes here:
1) Quota vs burst smoothing: our quota UI is aggregated per-minute or per-day; short spikes can still exhaust per-second token buckets even if you have aggregate quota remaining.
2) Interaction with continuous batching + client retries: the runtime batches short requests to improve throughput. When batch queueing increases queue_wait_ms, clients see higher latency and often retry aggressively. Those retries multiply load and can drive the token-bucket to 0 -> 429s. Customers often perceive this as "throttling" even though it's the retry feedback loop.

maya: adding runtime detail — we measure a small batch window (~10-40ms) for continuous batching. For lots of concurrent small requests the batch size grows but so does queue wait. Two actionable metrics to check: `runtime_queue_wait_ms` (p95) and `runtime_batch_size` (p95). If queue wait spikes before 429s, that's a signal of batching + retry amplification. Also check `kv_cache_hit_rate` for chat session workloads; cold-cache can increase per-request exec time and worsen queueing.

jeff: quick repro note: I was able to reproduce locally by hammering with 120 concurrent curl clients for 30s. The sequence I saw: queue_wait_ms climbs from ~5ms -> ~120ms, clients start timing out and retrying, then rate limit tokens drop to zero.

alex: For immediate customer mitigation: 
- Add client-side exponential backoff with jitter (e.g., base 100ms, max 2s).
- Limit concurrency from the client side (recommend capping to ~25-50 concurrent requests depending on model size).
- Consider using streaming responses to reduce perceived latency for the caller.

Also give these commands so we can correlate logs on our side: include the `x-redwood-request-id` header in a failing request and paste the full response headers + body. If you can run this quick check it will help: 

```bash
# a small sample that includes a unique request id header to correlate
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Customer-Trace: test-burst-2026-06" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-1","input":"ping","max_tokens":8}'
```

jane (customer): ok will run and paste headers. Any platform settings on our side we can tweak?

maya: two platform knobs to consider (we can toggle):
- per-route `max_concurrency` and `burst_window` — lowering max_concurrency reduces peak pressure, while a short burst_window increases how much short-term burst tolerance we allow.
- `sticky_routing_by_client_id` — if enabled and you provide an id header, requests for the same conversation tend to hit the same worker improving KV cache hit rate. That reduces backend exec time and decreases queue wait.

jeff: and a quick config snippet (internal) that we can apply as a temporary mitigation for this customer on hosted: 

```yaml
routes:
  - name: customer-jane-route
    match: /v1/generate
    max_concurrency: 40
    burst_window_ms: 5000  # allow short 5s bursts beyond steady rate
    enable_sticky_routing: true
    max_queue_ms: 500      # drop or 429 after 500ms queueing
```

alex: For longer-term fixes:
- Encourage warmup/priming calls for chat sessions to populate KV cache (send a short context when session starts).
- We can add client SDK helpers that implement concurrency limits + jittered backoff by default.
- On our end we can also increase per-second burst tokens for accounts that consistently need short bursts (we'll need an account-level request).

support-bot: Created INC-2026-0457 and assigned to eng-runtime.

alex: Action items:
- jane: run the `curl -v` test and paste failing headers + body (we'll correlate with rwd request id).
- maya/jeff: please pull `runtime_queue_wait_ms` p95, `runtime_batch_size` p95, `kv_cache_hit_rate` for timeframe 1777654300-1777654360 for the customer's tenant.
- support: offer to temporarily increase burst tokens for this customer while we tune routing/config.

jane (customer): pasted results in thread: `x-redwood-request-id: rwd_abc123` and `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0` on the first failing response. I'll accept a temporary increase if you can do it.

alex: thanks — we'll follow up in the ticket. In the meantime please add client-side backoff and reduce concurrency slightly; that usually mitigates the feedback loop fast. We'll post the prometheus snippets once we have them.

maya: note for internal docs: name this class of issue "perceived throttling" — it's the batching + retry amplification pattern. We should add a KB with recommended client limits and an SDK that enforces them.

jeff: I'll propose a short runtime change to expose `queue_wait_ms` as a routed header for tenant owner to observe (low friction) — added to the ticket.

alex: closing the thread here but keeping the ticket open. Thanks everyone.
